purpose: Candidate uses[] edges that were considered and REJECTED on editorial grounds. Scans that propose uses[] restorations (prose-corroboration, empty-uses completeness, declares-some-names-more, the §3b-cond rule-4 banner scan) must filter their candidates against this ledger, or they re-propose settled work every run. An entry here is a claim that a human or agent READ the blocks and concluded the edge does not belong -- it is not a claim that the target is unrelated.
why_this_exists: Forward-pointing candidates were triaged by DIRECTION and never by CONTENT, so a wrong edge could sit in the 'correct but blocked' pile indefinitely. rem:bsd-surreal-bound -> rem:rh-surreal-bound did exactly that for a whole work-arc: it was held as 'correct but forward' across three audits before anyone read the sentence that produced it, which turned out to say the two results GENERALIZE one another rather than depend.

reasons.overview-source: Source is a chapter overview (§0) block, typically a remark, that NAMES later results without depending on them. A survey previews; it does not require. Detected by reductio: satisfying such an edge proposes moving the target ahead of the introduction that previews it.
reasons.generalisation: Source generalises, specialises, or compares itself to the target. A generalisation does not depend on its own special case.
reasons.wrong-direction: The dependency is real but runs the other way; the reverse edge is the correct one.
reasons.restates-target: Source restates the target's entire content inline, so the reader need not leave the block.
reasons.future-work: Source names the target as work it explicitly does NOT do ('its proof would require ...').
reasons.aggregator: Source is an index/catalog/aggregator; the instances depend on it or it merely files them, so the edge runs the other way.
reasons.mis-aimed: The prose citation names the wrong block -- the cited content lives elsewhere (often the target's proof sibling). Retarget rather than declare.
reasons.author-ruling: Settled by the repo owner directly.

scan_filters.note: A scan proposing uses[] restorations must apply THREE filters before surfacing a candidate. Measured on the prn1 corroborated backlog (2026-08-11): 142 raw -> 93 after the first three -> 83 genuinely actionable. Roughly 40% of every run is otherwise re-proposed settled work.
scan_filters.1_rejection_ledger: The `rejections` list below. A JUDGEMENT that the edge does not belong, made by reading the blocks. Permanent, so it lives here. Removed 23 of 142.
scan_filters.2_foreshadows: content/<paper>/foreshadows.json. A target already recorded as a forward POINTER is not a uses[] dependency candidate. Removed 18 of 119.
scan_filters.3_transitive_reachability: COMPUTED, and deliberately NOT ledgered: drop any candidate A->T where T is already reachable from A through A's declared uses[] cone. The schema requires immediate neighbours only (types.ts: 'If A->B and B->C, then A lists only B'), so such an edge is redundant by construction. It must stay computed rather than recorded, because reachability is STATE-DEPENDENT: if the intermediate edge is later removed, the target stops being reachable and SHOULD be re-proposed. A ledger row would suppress it forever, which is wrong. Removed 10 of 93 -- all of them edges pruned in prn1 tranche 2 and re-surfaced by the next scan.
scan_filters.4_direction: Forward-pointing candidates are not uses[] edges; see the detangler criteria. Removed 8 of 101.
